items.title: Motorola’s Android 17 update fixes Android Auto connections on folded Razr phones
items.summary: No more flipping open your Razr every time you start your car.
items.body:
Affiliate links on Android Authority may earn us a commission. Learn more.

Mobile

Motorola's Android 17 update fixes Android Auto connections on folded Razr phones

No more flipping open your Razr every time you start your car.

•

Nov 25, 2026 — 8:18 AM ET

•

•

Ryan Haines / Android Authority

Add Android Authority on Google:

Preferred Source

Google Discover

TL;DR

• Motorola Razr owners report that the Android 17 update fixes a long-standing Android Auto connectivity bug.

• The issue emerged after the Android 16 update, forcing affected users to unfold their phones to establish a connection.

One convenience of owning a flip phone is being able to carry out everyday tasks without unfolding it. But for some Motorola Razr owners, even something as simple as connecting to Android Auto has required opening their phones since the Android 16 update. Thankfully, the latest Android 17 update appears to be putting an end to this frustration.

A Motorola Razr Ultra 2025 owner took to Reddit to share that Android Auto is once again connecting automatically while their phone is folded shut following the Android 17 update. Other owners in the thread have reported similar improvements.

The problem dates back several months. In February, a Razr Plus 2024 owner reported that their phone used to connect to their car wirelessly without even taking it out of their pocket. After installing Android 16, they had to flip open the phone every time they started their car. Neither changing Android Auto’s settings nor clearing app data and reinstalling updates helped. The phone didn’t even need to be unlocked for Android Auto to start working again. Simply unfolding it was enough.

Connectivity isn’t the only issue flip phone owners have experienced with Google’s driving platform. In September, we reported on a separate Android Auto bug that prevented Motorola Razr and Samsung Galaxy Z Flip owners from making outgoing calls through Gemini while their phones were folded shut.

It’s unclear whether Motorola’s Android 17 update addresses that problem, too. Nevertheless, it’s encouraging to see Razr owners regain some of the convenience they lost with Android 16, especially for a feature they potentially use every day.

Google Messages is testing a revamped voice messaging and media viewer interface

The app is also testing an updated media viewer with a larger viewing area and other tweaks.

•

Joe Maring / Android Authority

Add Android Authority on Google:

TL;DR

• Google Messages is testing an updated audio messaging interface with updated visuals and a progress indicator.

• The messaging app could also make it easier to set Voice Moods while recording, rather than waiting until after you finish.

• Google Messages is also working on a media viewer update, including new icons and a wider viewing area for photos and videos.

Google Messages is already working on voice messaging upgrades, and a future update could bring some more changes to that experience. Currently, the message card shows you an audio message’s overall duration, but it doesn’t tell you how far into the recording you are. Google Messages is working to remedy that.

APK teardown

This reporting is based on work-in-progress code. These features may not ship.

You're reading an Android Authority exclusive story you won’t find anywhere else. An APK teardown helps predict features that may arrive on a service in the future based on work-in-progress code. However, it is possible that such predicted features may not make it to a public release. More Authority Insights →

We dug into version 20261120_01 beta of Google Messages to enable a revamped audio message card that also shows a progress indicator. This helps you see how far along you are, especially for voice messages that are a couple of minutes long.

But that’s not the only upgrade that’s in development for voice messaging. Last week, we reported on the ability to set Voice Moods in Google Messages while recording, among other changes. We now have visuals on this particular upgrade as well.

In its current form, users can set Voice Moods only after they finish recording, as the first two screenshots above illustrate. Letting you choose from the available Voice Moods as you’re recording an audio message certainly seems like a logical upgrade. Additionally, there’s a dedicated close button (X) at the top right of this updated audio recording interface.

We’re also seeing the new “Send” button here in place of “Attach”, something we first learned about in a recent APK teardown. While this will undoubtedly speed up sending voice notes, it could also lead to users accidentally sending one when they didn’t intend to.

Beyond the changes coming to the voice recording interface, Google Messages is also testing a revised design for the photo/video viewer.

Among the changes we’re seeing is a larger media viewer that spans the width of the screen, replacing the current card-style viewer with rounded corners. The row of reactions sits in a pill-shaped container at the bottom, with only three visible in this redesign instead of four.

Meanwhile, the video playback controls are positioned just below the video rather than directly on it. Lastly, the existing Nano Banana icon for photos makes way for a contact icon bearing a familiar AI sparkle, while the message bubble icon for replies may be replaced by a reply icon (left-facing arrow).

As with most early revelations, it’s hard to predict when (or if) these design tweaks will roll out to the Messages app. In any case, we’ll keep a close eye on future app releases for more clues about these feature additions.

items.body:
Apple Has iPads Running macOS Internally, Says Gurman

Wednesday November 25, 2026 4:55 am PST by Tim Hardwick

Apple has iPads running macOS internally and has had them "for some time," according to Bloomberg's Mark Gurman, although he says no work is currently being done to bring the Mac operating system to iPads.

Speaking on his latest Power On podcast, Gurman said there is "no work being done to consumerize macOS on the iPad." Rather, Apple will continue to bring Mac features and apps like Final Cut to iPadOS piece by piece. Gurman also argued that per-operating-system EU regulation gives Apple an incentive to keep distinct systems for each device. Apple recently dismissed merging iPadOS and macOS.

Sony’s WH-1000XM4C have barely moved from their launch price since they arrived in the fall, until now. The M4 2nd Gen headphones are down to $198 on Amazon, a $102 (34%) discount on their $299.99 list price and a new all-time low.

The WH-1000XM4C are a refreshed version of Sony’s popular WH-1000XM4, keeping the same compact folding design and noise canceling while adding updated sound tuning. Bluetooth moves up to version 6.0, and Sony’s app now offers a 10-band EQ for fine-tuning the sound.

The battery can also be replaced, which should help them last longer. Sony rates battery life at up to 27 hours with noise canceling on and up to 34 hours with it off. A 3.5mm input lets you plug in a cable for wired listening, and Speak-to-Chat lowers your music automatically when you start talking. A full charge takes about three hours over USB-C, and you’ll need your own cable since one isn’t included in the box.

Touch controls on the right ear cup handle volume, track changes, and playback. At around 253g, they’re comfortable for long flights and workdays alike. Black, Platinum Silver, and Lavender are all at the same price, so you can pick whichever color suits you.

items.body:

Mobile

One UI 9.5 may try to sell you Samsung Care Plus if you drop your Galaxy phone

One UI 9.5 Beta 1 code shows Warranty Care uses drop sensor data to trigger protection plan ads without mentioning the fall.

•

Nov 25, 2026 — 6:38 AM ET

•

•

Shimul Sood / Android Authority

Add Android Authority on Google:

Preferred Source

Google Discover

TL;DR

• Code in One UI 9.5 Beta 1 shows Samsung’s Warranty Care app (v1.9.50.23) uses phone drop data to trigger Samsung Care Plus sales notifications.

• A single drop of 90cm or more onto a hard surface, or three drops of 60cm or more within 30 days, can trigger a default-on “Marketing” notification that doesn’t mention the fall.

• Drop logs remain stored locally on the device for 30 days. Signing up for Samsung Care Plus after a drop will usually not cover damage that has already occurred.

If you drop your Galaxy phone after updating to One UI 9.5, Samsung might follow up with a sales pitch for Samsung Care Plus. Code in the One UI 9.5 Beta 1 build for the Galaxy S26 Ultra shows that Samsung’s Warranty Care app will be able to use your Galaxy phone’s drop detection, including how far it fell and what it landed on, to decide when to recommend Samsung Care Plus. The notifications won’t mention the drop, though, and they arrive in a “Marketing” notification category that’s switched on by default.

Warranty Care is the app behind the “Warranty and care hub” in Settings. We first spotted the app hidden in an early One UI 9 build in March, and the Warranty hub debuted with One UI 9 on the Galaxy Z Fold 8 series before reaching the Galaxy S26 series. It puts your warranty status, diagnostics, repair bookings, and Samsung Care Plus sign-ups in one place, so you don’t have to dig through separate apps and websites when something goes wrong.

Samsung Newsroom

Recent Galaxy phones like the Galaxy S26 Ultra and Galaxy Z Fold 8 already know when you drop them. In One UI 9, a dedicated drop-classifier sensor reports each fall to the system, including how far the phone fell and whether it landed on a hard or soft surface, and the system logs it on the device. One UI 9.5 now connects that drop data to Warranty Care for a protection plan upsell.

APK teardown

This reporting is based on work-in-progress code. These features may not ship.

You're reading an Android Authority exclusive story you won’t find anywhere else. An APK teardown helps predict features that may arrive on a service in the future based on work-in-progress code. However, it is possible that such predicted features may not make it to a public release. More Authority Insights →

Your Galaxy phone’s drop sensor will soon be able to talk to Warranty Care

One UI 9 can already detect phone drops, and One UI 9.5 doesn’t change this. Instead, Samsung’s motion service for drop detection now passes data on each drop’s height and surface type to Warranty Care, and Warranty Care (v1.9.50.23 from One UI 9.5 Beta 1) is the only app on our Galaxy S26 Ultra that can receive it. The drop data appears locked to Samsung’s own system apps, so third-party apps will likely not be able to listen in. We also found the same sensor active on a Galaxy Z Fold 8, so the drop-based recommendations could reach more than just the Galaxy S26 series when One UI 9.5 rolls out.

Aamir Siddiqui / Android Authority

One UI 9’s version of Warranty Care (v1.9.03.2) has none of this.

Aamir Siddiqui / Android Authority

Each drop event includes two details: the height the phone fell from (in centimeters) and the type of surface it landed on (Hard, Soft, Unknown). Warranty Care also timestamps each drop event and stores it locally.

Aamir Siddiqui / Android Authority

Aamir Siddiqui / Android Authority

These drop events go into a dedicated table in Warranty Care’s local database.

How many drops before you get an ad for Samsung Care Plus?

Code within Warranty Care suggests it periodically checks its drop log against two rules:

• If your phone falls 90cm or more onto a hard surface at least once in 24 hours, it qualifies for a “high-impact drop” recommendation.

• If it falls 60cm or more onto a hard surface at least three times in 30 days, it qualifies for a “repeated drop” recommendation.

In the code snippet below, 86400000 is 24 hours written in milliseconds (24 x 60 x 60 x 1000), as Android measures time in milliseconds. The “j” variable refers to the current time, so “j – 86400000” refers to a drop that happened within the last 24 hours.

Aamir Siddiqui / Android Authority

Similarly, in the code snippet below, 2592000000 is 30 days (30 x 86400000):

Aamir Siddiqui / Android Authority

Falls onto soft surfaces, like a bed or a couch, or onto unknown surfaces don’t appear to count.

When either rule is met, Warranty Care can show one of these notifications:

Code

<string name="contextual_notification_s2_title">Protect your phone from falls</string>
<string name="contextual_notification_s2_body">Sign up for Samsung Care+ for protection against unexpected repair costs. Explore coverage options.</string>
<string name="contextual_notification_s3_title">Protect against accidental damage</string>
<string name="contextual_notification_s3_body">Sign up for Samsung Care+ for protection against unexpected repair costs. Explore coverage options.</string>

A cursory reading of the above strings will make you believe these are ordinary notifications. When you read between the lines, you will notice what these notifications don’t say. Neither of them mentions that your phone detected a drop. If you get one right after fumbling your phone on the sidewalk, the upsell notification may look like a well-timed coincidence, but the timing is the whole point.

Drops aren’t the only triggers for these upsell notifications. The same system can recommend Samsung Care Plus when you travel to a new country, after a completed repair, and as your enrollment window closes. The travel version reads: “Accidents can happen anywhere. Samsung Care+ covers repairs abroad.”

Samsung Care Plus pitches arrive as “Marketing” notifications, on by default

Warranty Care posts these Samsung Care Plus upsell recommendations (ad notifications) through its “Marketing” notification category, which sits alongside “General notices” and “Service and reservation.” The Marketing category is on by default and uses Android’s standard notification importance, so these pitches show up like any other regular notification.

From the code, we could spot some guardrails around these notifications in the current build, though there could be more:

• Only phones that are eligible for Samsung Care Plus but not yet enrolled get these recommendations. This narrows down the notification to recently purchased phones that are still within the sign-up window.

• You need to be signed in to a Samsung account and have accepted Warranty Care’s privacy notice, which appears when you first use features like requesting a repair.

• Recommendations are only sent between 9:00 AM and 8:00 PM. If one is due outside those hours, it waits until the next morning.

• Each drop-based recommendation can fire at most three times, and only one recommendation is active at a time.

• Samsung can switch these recommendations off remotely through a server-side flag.

What happens to your drop data?

From what we can see in the code, Warranty Care’s drop log doesn’t leave your phone. The app keeps drop events in its local database for 30 days and then deletes them. When a recommendation fires, the only thing sent to Samsung’s analytics is the recommendation type, such as “S2_HIGH_IMPACT_DROP,” not the height, surface, or time of the fall.

To be clear, your phone was already tracking drops before this change. In One UI 9, the system logs each fall on the device and passes it to Samsung’s on-device diagnostics service. What’s new in One UI 9.5 is that Warranty Care gets the same height and surface information and uses it to time Samsung Care Plus recommendations.

There’s also a curious line in Warranty Care that says it can personalize warranty information using “health activity and travel schedule data from Personal data intelligence.” We couldn’t find any code in this build that reads health or travel schedule data, and Warranty Care doesn’t currently appear in the Personal data intelligence app list on our Galaxy S26 Ultra. However, the travel recommendation is named “S5_UPCOMING_TRAVEL” internally, which hints that Samsung may want to time it around upcoming trips. For now, it appears to rely on detecting a country change instead.

Code

<string name="pdi_apps_to_enhance_description">Get personalized warranty and care information using health activity and travel schedule data from Personal data intelligence.</string>

The upsell notification will arrive after a drop, but Samsung Care Plus doesn’t cover past events

To be fair to Samsung, drop protection is exactly what Samsung Care Plus sells, and a nudge after a nasty fall is arguably more useful than a random ad. Still, most people won’t expect their phone’s fall sensor to decide when they see a sales pitch, especially when the notification doesn’t say why it appeared. A notification that says “We noticed your phone took a fall” would have been clearer and more transparent, though it would also reveal that the phone is tracking falls.

It’s worth remembering that Samsung Care Plus doesn’t cover damage that happened before you signed up. So if a drop has already cracked your screen, signing up after the notification won’t pay for that repair. It will only protect you from the next one. In the US, you can usually only add Samsung Care Plus when you buy your phone or within 60 days of purchase, apart from occasional open enrollment periods. Signing up later may require your phone to pass a device check first, which it might not if the drop has already damaged it.

If you’d rather not see these notifications when One UI 9.5 rolls out, go to Settings > Notifications > App notifications, tap the three-dot menu, and enable Show system apps. Then select Warranty and care > Notification categories and turn off Marketing. From what we can see in this One UI 9.5 Beta 1 build, Warranty Care still records drop events locally even if you turn off the notification category, since there’s no separate toggle for drop tracking.

We haven’t received one of these notifications on our Galaxy S26 Ultra yet, and Samsung could change or drop the feature before the stable One UI 9.5 release. We’ve reached out to Samsung for comment and will update this article when we hear back.

items.summary: Internal naming pattern offers clues about Samsung's plans.

Mobile

Samsung Galaxy Z TriFold 2 codename leak hints at another limited release

Internal naming pattern offers clues about Samsung's plans.

•

Nov 25, 2026 — 6:35 AM ET

•

•

Lanh Nguyen / Android Authority

Add Android Authority on Google:

Preferred Source

Google Discover

TL;DR

• Samsung is reportedly developing the Galaxy Z TriFold 2 under the codename Q9m.

• Samsung’s previous foldables with similar codename patterns never received global releases, suggesting the TriFold 2 could follow suit.

• Earlier reports pointed to increased TriFold production in 2027, but higher production volumes wouldn’t necessarily guarantee wider availability.

Samsung’s first Galaxy Z TriFold was a $2,899 smartphone that many people couldn’t buy even if they could afford it. The phone was sold in limited quantities across a handful of markets before Samsung pulled the plug just months after launch. Those hoping its successor, the Galaxy TriFold 2, would be easier to get their hands on may be in for another disappointment, according to a fresh leak.

According to Dutch publication GalaxyClub, Samsung is developing its second-generation TriFold under the codename Q9m. The upcoming Galaxy Z Fold 9 and Fold 9 Ultra carry the H9 and Q9 codenames, respectively. Rather than assigning the TriFold 2 a distinct codename, Samsung appears to be treating it as a variation of the Fold 9 Ultra, at least internally.

The seemingly insignificant letter at the end of the codename could tell us quite a bit about Samsung’s plans for the phone. Consider how Samsung has named its previous foldables internally:

• 2024: Galaxy Z Fold 6 (Q6) and Galaxy Z Fold Special Edition (Q6a).

• 2025: Galaxy Z Fold 7 (Q7) and Galaxy Z TriFold (Q7m).

• 2026: Galaxy Z Fold 8 (H8) and Galaxy Z Fold 8 Ultra (Q8).

• 2027: Galaxy Z Fold 9 (H9), Galaxy Z Fold 9 Ultra (Q9), and Galaxy Z TriFold 2 (Q9m).

Both the Fold Special Edition and the original TriFold shared their parent devices’ codenames with an extra letter. Neither launched globally. Meanwhile, this year’s two Fold models received entirely different codenames, and both enjoyed global releases. Based on this pattern, GalaxyClub suspects the TriFold 2 could once again be destined for select markets, with European buyers potentially missing out for the second time.

Earlier reports suggested Samsung was planning to significantly ramp up TriFold 2 production in 2027. However, the smartphone industry’s worsening memory shortage complicates that outlook. Samsung has reportedly cut its overall smartphone shipment target from 232 million units this year to 210 million in 2027, although it’s unclear whether this reduction will affect its foldable lineup.

There’s also no indication that the TriFold 2 is specifically affected by these cuts, but even if Samsung ramps up production, that doesn’t necessarily mean the phone will be available in more countries.

With the next generation of Samsung foldables not expected until summer 2027, there’s still plenty of time for more encouraging news to emerge. Hopefully, buying Samsung’s most ambitious foldable won’t remain a privilege determined by where you live.

I've used the Pixel 11 Pro XL for months, and I wouldn't go without these 6 accessories

Keeping my Pixel spoiled and charged.

•

•

•

Shimul Sood / Android Authority

Add Android Authority on Google:

Preferred Source

Google Discover

I’ve been using the Google Pixel 11 Pro XL since it launched globally in August, and after a few months, I’ve started paying closer attention to how well it holds up over time. Buying an expensive smartphone is one thing, but keeping it in good condition months or even years later takes a little more effort. No matter how careful I am, daily use eventually takes a toll, whether it’s a scratch, an accidental drop, or the battery slowly losing its ability to hold a charge.

I’ve realized that something as simple as using a good case, protecting the screen, and being mindful of how I charge my phone can go a long way in keeping it in good shape. Over the past few months, I’ve also figured out which accessories are actually worth spending money on. So, if you’ve recently bought a Pixel 11 Pro XL, here are six accessories I’d recommend investing in to keep your phone looking and working at its best for as long as possible.

Readers' poll

Which accessory do you think is most important for keeping a phone in good shape?

12 votes

The right case makes all the difference

Shimul Sood / Android Authority

The first accessory I’d recommend getting for your Pixel is a good case. Apart from protecting your phone from accidental drops and scratches, a case can also change how your phone looks and feels in your hand. I’ve been switching between two Mous cases on my Pixel 11 Pro XL: the Moss Super Thin case and the Limitless Black Leather case.

The Moss Super Thin case is easily my favorite for looks.

TL;DR

• Samsung appears to have changed how it displays stats for multiple activities in a single session.

• Previously, it would stack details and show them collectively after a workout.

• But now, it is reportedly only showing stats from the last activity.

A workout at a gym may involve more than one activity, which is why smartwatches such as the Galaxy Watch let you record a series of workouts or create custom routines. At the end of the workout, it shows the entire duration of your workout along with the calories burned. However, Samsung may have recently changed how the Galaxy Watch displays these stats, leaving regular users upset.

items.body: Anthropic has released a new feature for Claude that allows users to install artifacts as desktop apps on macOS and Windows. Artifacts are documents, designs, dashboards, and interactive tools that Claude creates in a panel alongside your chat, where you can view and edit them. When you ask Claude to create an artifact, you can now click "Install as app" in the Share menu, after which you'll be able to launch it in its own dedicated app window and see it in the Dock. Artifact-based apps don't need to be packaged or signed, but they do need a permission level to be set. Choosing Default permissions means they can only do what they'd be able to do in a browser, while giving them higher App permissions means they can do things like create always-on-top windows, listen for global keyboard shortcuts, and send notifications. Full computer access means apps can run programs and read, change or delete files without asking each time. Apps can be used with connectors, and they include an option to add a menu bar item. Apps also update automatically when the underlying artifact is edited, and each change prompts a new permissions request. Anthropic has made some example apps available to try and to give users an idea of what's possible. Anthropic says building an app and any calls it makes to Claude count toward usage limits. The feature remains in beta and is available on all plans in Claude Desktop, though Enterprise users will need to switch it on manually first. TL;DR

• Google is rolling out support for capturing multiple photos at once with the AI Mode camera.

• It replaces the shutter button with a plus icon and lets users attach up to 10 images at once.

• The change is rolling out with the latest version of the Google app.

Google has been steadily adding input options to AI Mode in the Google app. We’ve seen Google working to add PDF uploads to AI Mode and even a share sheet shortcut for attaching files. Now, we’ve spotted the company rolling out yet another small but useful change to the AI Mode camera.

In the latest version of the Google app (v17.78.13), the camera in AI Mode’s compose box is getting an upgrade. Until now, the Lens icon in AI Mode opened a camera interface that let you capture and attach an image for AI Mode queries. If you wanted to add another, you had to open the camera interface again. That’s now changing. The camera interface now has a plus button in place of the usual shutter button. You can tap it once to capture an image, then tap it again to capture another.

Captured photos show up as small thumbnails above the button, with an “X” icon to remove any images you don’t want. When you’re done, tap “Add photos” to attach everything to the compose box in one go.

You can capture and attach up to 10 images this way. Once added, the images sit in the compose box, and you can type your question as usual.

This can be helpful when you want to ask AI Mode about multiple things at once, like comparing several products or identifying multiple items in a single query. It also removes an annoying bit of friction from the AI Mode camera experience.

The new feature is already rolling out with the latest Google app update. However, it seems to be a server-side update, so merely updating the Google app on your phone doesn’t guarantee the new feature. That said, it appears to be rolling out widely and is already available on several of our devices.

items.title: ChatGPT and Codex will share usage limits for paid users starting in December
items.summary: Using one AI tool could limit how much you can use another.
items.body:

General technology

ChatGPT and Codex will share usage limits for paid users starting in December

Using one AI tool could limit how much you can use another.

•

Nov 25, 2026 — 4:37 AM ET

•

•

Edgar Cervantes / Android Authority

Add Android Authority on Google:

Preferred Source

Google Discover

TL;DR

• Starting in December, ChatGPT, Work, and Codex will share a single usage allowance across Plus, Pro, and Business plans.

• Usage will be measured in tokens rather than messages, with more advanced models and complex tasks consuming more of your allowance.

• Instant chat will be exempt from the shared allowance, but OpenAI hasn’t disclosed how large the new limits will be.

ChatGPT has grown into much more than a chatbot, with OpenAI introducing tools like Work and Codex to help users tackle everything from building presentations to developing apps. Until now, you could use these tools without worrying about how they would affect your regular ChatGPT allowance. But as OpenAI brings Chat and Work together, it’s also changing how much you can do with your paid subscription.

OpenAI’s Thibault Sottiaux announced on X that the company has begun rolling out the combined Chat and Work experience to a small group of Pro users ahead of a wider release. However, a new support page reveals the catch that didn’t make it into the announcement. Starting in December, ChatGPT and Codex will share a usage allowance across Plus, Pro, and Business plans.

Stephen Radochia / Android Authority

Currently, Work and Codex already share usage limits, while regular ChatGPT conversations have their own. You could exhaust your Codex allowance building an app and still switch to ChatGPT’s Thinking models to discuss ideas or work through complex questions. Come December, those activities will draw from the same pot.

OpenAI is also changing how it measures usage. Rather than counting messages, the company will measure consumption in tokens, the small chunks of information AI models read and generate. Asking ChatGPT a relatively simple question using a Thinking model could consume considerably less of your allowance than asking it to analyze a lengthy document.

This means spending hours coding with Codex could leave you with less room to use ChatGPT for other demanding tasks, such as deep research. Similarly, heavy ChatGPT usage could limit how much coding you can get done with Codex. The good news, however, is that Instant chat won’t count toward the shared allowance. You’ll still be able to use ChatGPT for everyday conversations without eating into your budget for more demanding tasks.

OpenAI expects most users won’t hit their limits as often as they do today, but it hasn’t revealed how large the combined allowances will be. You’ll be able to track your remaining usage under Settings > Usage and purchase credits for eligible features, upgrade your plan, or wait for a reset when you run out.

Some users may see these changes before December as OpenAI gathers feedback.

items.title: I didn’t realize how useful Google Contacts was until I used these 5 features
items.summary: I was missing out on some of the app's best features.
items.body:

Mobile

I didn't realize how useful Google Contacts was until I used these 5 features

I was missing out on some of the app's best features.

•

Nov 25, 2026 — 4:30 AM ET

•

•

Megan Ellis / Android Authority

Add Android Authority on Google:

Preferred Source

Google Discover

Google Contacts is an app that I’ve simultaneously used and ignored for years. It’s always on my device because I use it to sync phone numbers and email addresses to my Google Account so that I always have a backup, but I’d rarely explored its distinct features until recently. That’s when I realized just how much you can do in the app.

In particular, several features have turned the app into a powerful way for me to manage contact information.

Readers' poll

Which Google Contacts feature do you like the most?

22 votes

Weather and time info

Megan Ellis / Android Authority

I didn’t realize that Google Contacts had this feature until I was trying out ways to replicate Pixel VIPs on other devices. If you have an address saved for a person, their page in the Google Contacts app will update with their local time and weather. This works even if you just have a suburb saved for the contact — so you don’t have to add their exact home location.

This feature works particularly well for contacts who live in another time zone or people you visit often. For example, by having my brother’s suburb in Ireland saved, I can double-check the time there before messaging him without having to use a time zone calculator or figure out whether Ireland is currently on summer time.

This feature is great for contacts who live in different time zones or areas with a different climate.

Meanwhile, for friends who live in other parts of Cape Town, I can check whether I need to bring a coat before I visit them since the weather can be wildly different depending on where you live in the city. This is especially true when it comes to wind and rain.

To add an address for a contact, follow these steps:

1. Open a contact’s page by tapping their name in the app

2. Tap the pen icon. Scroll down and select Address.

3. Type in their location and then select Save.

4. After some time, the location field will update with the weather and time information. If it’s not updating, tap on the arrow icon to open Google Maps and exit again, and the field should update.

Birthday and important date reminders

Megan Ellis / Android Authority

Besides the birthdays I’ve known since childhood, keeping track of important dates and anniversaries is difficult for me. For a long time, I relied on Facebook to notify me when it is a friend’s birthday. But as I use the social media site less, and people I know delete their accounts, this method hasn’t been reliable.

That’s why I was glad to find out that I can add birthdays and important date reminders to Google Contacts. These dates also sync with my Google Calendar, adding a bit of redundancy for extra reassurance that I don’t miss an important date.

With this feature, I don't have to rely on Facebook to remember the birthdays of important contacts.

This feature requires you to save the contact to your Google Account and you need to add the notification at least 24 hours before the date. You also need to enable notifications in the Google Contacts app. The feature lets you choose the day you receive the notification from a range of options.

To add a birthday or important date for a contact:

1. Open the contact page and select Reminders.

2. Select New reminder.

3. Choose the type of reminder from the available labels (Birthday, Anniversary, or Custom) and then choose the date.

4. Set the date and time you want to receive your reminder. Then, select Save.

5. You will see a small message box that notes that the reminder has been saved.

Notes

Megan Ellis / Android Authority

Many of us will be familiar with the habit of adding descriptive terms to a contact’s name so that you remember who they are. I have countless contacts with words like “neighbor,” “courier,” “landlord,” or the company where they work added to the name in brackets. But the Notes feature in Google Contacts means that you can keep the contact name tidy without a bunch of terms added after their actual name.

The Notes field is also helpful for general notes about a contact, and it’s one of the fields that Pixel VIPs surfaces. You can use it to add gift ideas, remember your friend’s favorite color, or write down any other useful information. You don’t have to rely on your memory.

Notes provide a helpful place to jot down important details you want to remember about your contact.

This will also make it easier when it comes time to clean up your contacts, since you can easily figure out if you still need to message that person in the future. For example, there have been a few times I’ve needed to take down the number of a company driver when I’m at a press event. These contacts are only relevant for one day, yet they stay in the app years later.

To add a note to a contact:

1. Tap the pen icon on a contact page.

2. Scroll down to the Notes field.

3. Type in the details you want to add and tap on Save.

4. You will now be able to see notes on their page below their main contact details.

Custom field

Megan Ellis / Android Authority

At first, I figured that Custom field simply duplicates what Notes can do in Google Contacts. But I realized pretty quickly that the Notes section can become cluttered if you depend on it significantly. That’s where the Custom field feature comes in handy. It allows you to add more information to a contact’s page in a structured way, without creating a long wall of text. It also prioritizes this information at the top of the page, along with their contact details.

This works best for fields that you want to repeat across different contacts. For example, you might want to save social media pages for business contacts depending on your industry, or you may just want to remember how you met someone. Custom fields are specifically there to fill in the gaps that other fields like Website, Job title, and Related people don’t cover.

A Custom field lets you add extra information to your contact that displays near the top of their profile.

For example, for neighbors, I can use the custom field feature to list which unit they live in within my complex. For friends that I know from online games, I can add their gamer tag if I don’t want to save it as their nickname. Because you determine the title of the field and the text included, the possibilities are endless.

To create a custom field for a contact:

1. Select the pen icon on their contact page to edit their profile.

2. Scroll down and select Other > Custom field.

3. Add the title in Custom field and the label in Custom label. Then tap Save.

4. The Custom field will now appear below their contact details on their profile.

Your info

Megan Ellis / Android Authority

Google Contacts is perfect for saving the contact information of others, but you can also use it to edit and share your own. I find this more convenient than trying to edit my details using the Google Account personal info page, especially since it’s right at the top of the Google Contacts app. It’s also specifically focused on information that you want to share with others, rather than information Google has about you.

On the Your info page, you can change your profile picture (which will be visible to others), add contact details like your phone and email, and add additional information like your address and certain fields. These fields aren’t as extensive as those available for your saved contacts. You can add Company, Department, Job title, and Website. However, you can also add your nickname when you edit your display name.

The Your info page makes it easy to share your details with someone else, using methods like Quick Share.

You can then use the sharing feature to share your details with others. Google Contacts allows you to select which details you choose to share, which is particularly helpful. You can share these details using Quick Share or a messaging app. The recipient can then open these details in their own contacts app.

To edit your details in the Your info page, simply use the pen icon. If you want to share your details with someone else:

1. Tap the Share icon.

2. Select the details you want to share by selecting Choose details to share, and then tap Share.

3. Select the sharing method for your contact file.

After diving into these Google Contacts features, I realized that there’s a lot more going on in the app than I expected. Over the years, the app has become more feature-rich, even including shortcuts to features like location sharing and navigation.

The features I’ve discussed stand out in particular because they’ve changed the way I view the app. If you haven’t tried them, I recommend checking them out to see how you can put them to use.

The smartphone market is bracing for troubled times ahead.

TL;DR

• Most major phone makers have reportedly lowered their 2027 shipment targets due to rising memory costs.

• Xiaomi and vivo are cutting the most, by 25% and 29% respectively, while Apple and Samsung are also reducing their targets.

• HONOR is the only major phone brand that’s not reducing its shipment target for 2027.

The memory shortage has been a theme throughout this year, and we’ve seen several manufacturers hike phone prices because of it. Now, it seems to be hitting manufacturers’ sales plans as well.

According to a report from Jiemian News, citing supply chain sources, most major smartphone makers have finalized their shipment targets for 2027 and expect to sell considerably fewer phones next year.

The steepest cuts are reportedly coming from vivo and Xiaomi, going from 85 million units in 2026 to 60 million in 2027 for vivo and from 120 million down to 90 million in 2027 for Xiaomi. That’s a reduction of 29% and 25%, respectively. Motorola is aiming for 40 million unit sales next year, down 20% from 50 million in 2026. OPPO has also reportedly finalized a target of 90 million units — a 14% drop from its 2026 sales target.

Aamir Siddiqui / Android Authority

Meanwhile, Samsung and Apple are cutting less. The South Korean giant is reportedly aiming for 210 million units, down 9.5% from 232 million, while Apple is dropping 5.6% from 233 million to 220 million units.

The only exception, according to the report, is HONOR. It’s reportedly sticking with 50 million units for 2027, the same as this year. At the HONOR 700 series launch, CEO Li Jian said that mid-range phones face bigger cost pressures than flagships, and that HONOR plans to keep pushing while others pull back. These higher cost pressures, coupled with price hikes, also made flagship phones look like a better deal than mid-range phones, and they became more popular this year. The report also cites IDC data showing that HONOR was the only leading Chinese phone brand to grow shipments quarter-on-quarter in Q3.

Stephen Schenck / Android Authority

Li Jian also said some phones have been downgraded in chips, cameras, or memory to hold prices steady as the memory shortage worsens and prices skyrocket. In fact, a recent Counterpoint report stated that DRAM revenue in Q3 2026 approached $200 billion, growing 369% year-on-year due to AI server demand.

Smartphone shipments throughout 2026 have been on a rough-and-tumble ride. Earlier this year, companies like Xiaomi, OPPO, and vivo reported double-digit declines in sales due to rising memory costs.

It seems 2027 will bring more of the same, with only HONOR holding out some hope for its portfolio. Meanwhile, the memory shortage is expected to continue into 2028, according to the report. Any reprieve from heavily inflated prices and dwindling sales is expected only toward the end of 2027 or in early 2028.

It’s been several months since Android 17 made its mainstream debut, but as of October 2026, a tiny percentage of devices were running it. As is so often the case, it takes a while for the latest version of Google’s mobile OS to proliferate across devices, but it’s particularly worrying that nearly four months after launch, just 1% of devices were running it.

We just had to know if these broader Android Studio figures matched those of our readers. So, we ran a poll, asking readers which Android version their device is running. The results are in, and it’s a completely different story.

Nearly three in every five devices (58.2%) are running Android 17, which is certainly a stark difference from the 1% indicated by Android Studio in October. This suggests Google’s and other manufacturers’ update rollouts are progressing well, and that Android Authority readers are generally running devices that are either brand new or still on their extended software update plans.

Android 16 accounts for 15.5% of polled readers’ devices, and was the only other version to receive double-digit support. Android 15, 14, and 13 followed closely behind and are running on 13.4% of devices combined.

TL;DR

• Gemini Notebook can now incorporate images from uploaded study materials into flashcards, making visual learning easier.

• Google has added an optional stopwatch to flashcard review sessions to help users practice recalling information under time pressure.

• You can now schedule flashcard review reminders through the Gemini mobile app, and all three improvements are available without a paid subscription.

Google has been adding some interesting features to Gemini Notebook lately. Just a few days ago, we reported that the tool could turn your research materials into interactive websites. Now, Google is improving the flashcard experience with three new features that could make studying more effective and, perhaps more importantly, easier to keep up with.

The first change addresses a limitation of text-based flashcards. Gemini Notebook can now pull relevant images from your uploaded study materials and incorporate them into flashcards. This should be handy for subjects where visual references matter. For instance, if you’re studying human anatomy, identifying different parts of the heart from a diagram could be much more effective than memorizing their names from a wall of text.

Another addition is an optional stopwatch that lets you time your flashcard review sessions. Remembering the correct answer is one thing, but recalling it quickly in an exam hall is another. For example, you could challenge yourself to work through a deck of flashcards in five minutes and gradually see how much faster you get with repeated practice.

Tushar Mehta / Android Authority

Arguably, the most practical addition of the three is scheduling flashcard review reminders through the Gemini mobile app. Creating flashcards is easy enough, but remembering to revisit them regularly is where many of us struggle. You could now set up a reminder to review your French vocabulary every evening or brush up on your notes during your morning commute.

What’s nice is that these improvements extend well beyond the classroom. Whether you’re learning a new language, preparing for a job interview, or working toward a professional certification, Gemini Notebook is becoming an increasingly compelling alternative to dedicated flashcard apps.

Better yet, Google isn’t locking these improvements behind a paid subscription. All three features are now available to users with personal Google accounts, Google Workspace customers, and Workspace Individual subscribers.

Gemini’s floating overlay now helps you compare prices, check warranty terms across shopping apps

Gemini overlay uses screen context and recommends actions while using shopping apps on Android.

•

•

•

Akshay Gangwar / Android Authority

Add Android Authority on Google:

Preferred Source

Google Discover

TL;DR

• Gemini’s floating overlay on Android now uses screen context to find the best shopping deals across apps.

• You can ask it to check if a product is worth considering or compare prices across different apps.

• The feature works by grabbing a screenshot of the page behind it but doesn’t require you to share your screen with Gemini Live.

Google already curates products from multiple online stores in the Shopping section of its search results. If you’d rather skip manually scouring products, you can ask Gemini or Google’s AI Mode to recommend or filter them based on your preferences. Now, Google is making these insights even more accessible with prompts on top of any popular shopping app on your phone.

Google is starting to roll out new shopping help prompts right via the Gemini overlay. When you open Gemini over a product page on a shopping app, it will now suggest prompts such as “Help me pick,” “Compare prices,” or “Check warranty and returns.” Tapping any prompt makes Gemini take a screenshot of the product page and use it as context along with the text prompt. For instance, when you ask it to compare prices, it will compare the current listing, say Amazon, against other online retailers, such as Walmart and Target, which can be useful for holiday shopping, especially for the ongoing Black Friday and Cyber Monday sales.

The ability to analyze your screen isn’t at all new for Gemini — the feature has been around for over two years. Last December, Google also expanded Gemini’s ability to scan what’s on your screen to deliver better results, even without you having to share your screen with Gemini Live. However, this is the first time we’re noticing shopping-specific contextual suggestions.

Gemini overlay uses a more verbose versions of these suggestions to prompt itself in chat. All of these conversations also appear in your Gemini chat history, and you can revisit them later.

That said, unlike PDFs, web pages, or YouTube videos, where Gemini can scan the entire media, shopping context will be limited to what’s visible on the screen and not what you would see when you scroll the page. Google has yet to update its support page for ways Gemini helps with shopping, but we anticipate the feature will work across multiple different shopping apps. We can confirm it works with Amazon, Flipkart, and even quick commerce apps such as Blinkit.

The feature is already live with version 17.78.13 of the Google app and is likely part of a server-side rollout.

Another feature arriving with the latest version is the ability to mute Gemini Live’s voice output and get written responses (through captions) without having to type themselves. This lets users continue having verbal conversations with Gemini Live without disturbing others nearby, all without muting their mic or turning down the phone’s volume. We discovered this feature last month when we also found out about Google’s new, dazzling Gemini Live UI, but that has yet to go live.

AssembleDebug / Android Authority

To mute Gemini’s responses during a Live chat, you can tap the speaker icon in the top-right corner of the screen.

items.body:

Mobile

Samsung promises One UI 9.5 will fix rapidly declining battery health on Galaxy phones

Premature battery wear or a software error?

•

Nov 25, 2026 — 3:09 AM ET

•

•

Brady Snyder / Android Authority

Add Android Authority on Google:

Preferred Source

Google Discover

TL;DR

• Some Galaxy users have reported unusually rapid drops in battery health following the One UI 9.0 update.

• Samsung support says the upcoming One UI 9.5 update will address the issue.

• It’s unclear whether the problem stems from inaccurate battery health readings or accelerated battery degradation.

Battery life has been a sore point for some Galaxy owners since Samsung rolled out One UI 9.0, with users reporting increased battery drain on the Galaxy S24 and S25 series. But another battery-related concern has emerged following the update: unusually rapid drops in reported battery health. Luckily, Samsung support now says the upcoming One UI 9.5 update will address the issue.

In a post on Samsung’s Turkish community forum, a Galaxy user shared a response they received after submitting an error report through Samsung Members. The support representative explicitly stated that the battery health deterioration issue would be addressed with One UI 9.5. Here’s a Google Translate version:

The issue of decreased battery health you’re experiencing will be addressed with the upcoming One UI 9.5 update.

According to the user, battery health percentages have been dropping abnormally since the One UI 9.0 update, with some devices reportedly showing 94% battery health after just a month of use. The response came approximately two weeks after the user submitted their error report.

Alfatürk / Samsung Turkey community

Samsung introduced detailed battery health information with the Galaxy S25 series, giving owners more insight into how their batteries age. However, that information is only useful if the figures are accurate.

What’s unclear from Samsung’s response is whether One UI 9.0 is causing batteries to degrade faster than expected or whether there’s a software bug causing phones to underestimate their remaining battery capacity. While One UI 9.5 could correct inaccurate readings or address software issues contributing to premature battery wear, no software update can restore battery capacity that has already been physically lost.

The good news is that One UI 9.5 is already in beta, with the stable version expected to debut alongside the Galaxy S27 series in a couple of months. Granted, Galaxy owners experiencing abnormal drops in battery health may not have to wait much longer for a fix.
